page.layout: One column of text on a single printed page, with questions (I.) set in roman and answers (R.) set in italic, each pair as its own block; no margin notes; a catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: I. Quid vetatur à Domino octauo præ-cepto?

p.i: R. Omnes rapinæ, omnia furta, omnis iniusti-tia, quibus simplicium innocentia circumuenitur, omnis calliditas, versutia, & violenta direptio.

main_text.p: R. Mendacia damnantur, maledicentia, con-uitia, contumeliæ, quibus fama fratris no-stri proscinditur.
I. Dic quæ sunt prohibita 10. lege.

p.i: R. Dilige Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde, ex toto animo, ex omnibus viribus tuis: & proximum tuum vt teipsum. Quæcunq; vultis vt faciant vobis homines, eadem facite & illis.

main_text.p: I. Quis dat vires vt seruemus hæc præcepta?

p.i: R. Solus Deus per Christum, cui fi credimus effundit charitatem in corda nostra, & scribit præcepta Dei in cor.

page.notes: Catchword "Was" read at the lower right; the first letter of the last syllable is partly obscured, so the reading is doubtful. The numbering "I." for questions is likely a printed "Q." or "I." in the Latin catechism style, copied as printed. Some letters in the italic answers, notably "i" and "f" in "fi", are uncertain; "cui fi" is printed as shown.
